paper.title_en: Topological multicomponent superconductivity with sizable $s$-wave admixture in twisted bilayer cuprates
paper.abstract_en: We investigate multicomponent superconductivity in twisted bilayer cuprates with order parameter $s+d_1 e^{iφ_1}+d_2 e^{iφ_2}$, where $s=s_1+s_2$ is the layer-symmetric $s$-wave pairing and $d_i$ is the $d$-wave pairing in layer $i$. When $φ_1-φ_2\neq 0,π$, this three-component state spontaneously breaks time-reversal and $C_4$ rotational symmetries and can realize a topologically nontrivial phase. Ginzburg-Landau analysis and self-consistent mean-field calculations show that this state is stabilized over a broad parameter regime. We further identify nematic Kerr anisotropy as a key signature distinguishing it from $s+id$ and $d_1+e^{iφ}d_2$, and find that its Josephson critical current remains sizable near the $45^{\circ}$ twist. Our results show that $s$-wave pairing does not preclude chiral topological superconductivity, pointing to twisted cuprates as a more robust platform than previously appreciated.
